newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian economic growth at 2.08 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Colombian economic growth at 2.08 pct in 1996.

text.p: Colombia's economy grew 2.08 percent in 1996, its lowest expansion since 1991 when growth for the year was 2.0 percent, a government report said.
The report, by the National Statistics Department (DANE), noted that last year's slowdown followed bubbling economic growth rates of 5.36 percent in 1995 and 5.8 percent in 1994.
The government had forecast GDP growth of 3.5 percent in 1996. But DANE said a number of factors, including a recession in the construction sector, slowed the economy.
The manufacturing sector suffered negative growth of -2.86 percent in 1996 compared with growth of 1.01 percent in 1995 and 1.6 percent in 1994, according to DANE.
It said the hardest hit areas of the industrial sector were those linked to the building sector.

Surveys conducted by private business groups over the last year have repeatedly cited political uncertainty, and the scandal over charges that President Ernesto Samper used drug money to finance his 1994 campaign, among the reasons for the economic slowdown in 1996.

Colombia's economic growth rate averaged 4.5 percent between 1985-1995 and the government target for 1997 is GDP growth of 4.0 to 4.5 percent. Independent analysts forecast growth of no more than about 3.5 percent, however.
